title: Cardiac Rhythm Disturbances

source.boundary: Actual Chapter18 title in lower-right column PDF47/printed99, below Chapter17 references; through full left column and upper-right continuation and REFERENCES notice PDF71/printed123, above actual Chapter19 title in right column. Running headers are not boundaries.
source.verification: Author checked hash/source/boundaries. Main independently verified all16 term/page matches, actual rendered boundaries, source-match types, cue economy and reuse. Main corrected long QT source type to Table18-27. Vocabulary location only, not clinical or recall validation.

scope: Sixteen selected reusable vocabulary terms from a long chapter, not exhaustive coverage or a salience ranking. Offline candidate associations only, not clinical anchors, narration or image-generation prompts. New compositions are not necessarily new primitives or novel inventions.

source_wording_notes.atrial fibrillation: Shares the ATRIAL FIBRILLATION AND ATRIAL FLUTTER heading on printed106; also exact body match there.
source_wording_notes.atrial flutter: Shares the ATRIAL FIBRILLATION AND ATRIAL FLUTTER heading on printed106; also exact body match there.
source_wording_notes.Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome: Exact full heading on printed118. White wolf in a parking bay adds a parking/Parkinson learned association, not an exact full-name sound rebus.
source_wording_notes.long QT syndrome: Selected occurrence on printed122 is the Table18-27 title/table, not a standalone chapter heading/body occurrence; corrected following main source audit.
source_wording_notes.amiodarone: Selected from Table18-2 on printed101, not its dosing or treatment instructions. Earlier Chapter11 hold remains unresolved.

entries.cue: Heart character sprinting with conspicuous speed streaks.
entries.reason: Reuse the established sprinting-heart family, not a tacky syllable puzzle. No rate, rhythm subtype, exercise advice or cause encoded.

entries.cue: Heart character riding a familiar slow snail.
entries.prior: New contrast composition using the heart/speed ingredients in docs/chapter-13-cue-audit.json#tachycardia; not a new heart primitive.
entries.reason: User-proposed snail makes the slow token more legible in a still image than a slow step. Editorial contrast only, untested; no rate cutoff, symptom, diagnosis or action recommendation.

entries.cue: Sick-looking sine-wave character holding a thermometer prop, separate from any clinical monitor.
entries.cue_scope: Sick plus sine/sinus learned name bridge
entries.reason: Preserves prior partial sound bridge; does not revive workshop sign/noose fragments. Thermometer is wordplay, not a symptom, and character is not an ECG.

entries.cue: Tied bundle of tree branches visibly stopped at a barrier.
entries.reason: Same phrase composition, no conduction anatomy, side qualifier, ECG criteria or mechanism.

entries.cue: Very long pool cue beside a cup of tea.
entries.reason: Keep established length contrast with short QT; not an ECG interval, threshold or diagnosis.

entries.cue: Very short pool cue beside a cup of tea, staged identically to the long-cue version.
entries.reason: Same paired family; only cue length changes. No interval, value or clinical interpretation.

entries.cue: Ribbon visibly twisted around recognizable ballet pointe shoes.
entries.reason: Preserve existing learned name bridge, not rhythm morphology, mechanism or treatment.

entries.cue: Schematic flat trace beside a still heart token.
entries.reason: Same category cue; a flat display is not proof of diagnosis or a monitor-confirmation instruction.
Reuse the existing Chapter1 double meaning carried forward in Chapter11 rather than invent another heart-arrest symbol. No physiology or treatment.

entries.cue: Drummer visibly outside the circle occupied by the rest of a band.
entries.cue_scope: Out-of-place plus musical beats; learned ectopic family cue
entries.prior: New composition using familiar drummer and group-position ingredients; no matching whole-term cue located in prior chapter banks/catalog/workshops checked.
entries.reason: Familiar relational wordplay, not a map of cardiac origin or a clinical rhythm pattern. Offstage/solo-drummer ambiguity requires taught context, not a claim of isolated diagnostic specificity.

entries.cue: Drummer at a conspicuous road junction.
entries.prior: New composition; shares the drummer/beat ingredient with ectopic beats in this bank, not a separate beat primitive.
entries.reason: Uses a familiar place and musical role. Road junction is not cardiac anatomy or a propagation route; the two drummer compositions need learned-context discrimination.

entries.cue: Conspicuously fluttering cloth pennant beside a heart token.
entries.cue_scope: Flutter headword in an already identified atrial-rhythm lesson
entries.prior: New composition using a familiar flutter action and existing heart ingredient; no new cardiac primitive.
entries.reason: Broad learned action cue; atrial location is supplied by lesson context, not hidden in the pennant. No waveform, rate, rhythm distinction or physiological animation claimed.

entries.cue: A loose fringe of fine fibers beside a heart token.
entries.cue_scope: Fiber/fibril root reminder within an atrial-fibrillation lesson
entries.prior: New composition using the existing heart ingredient and a familiar fringe; not a new unique fibrillation primitive validated across lessons.
entries.reason: Partial learned root bridge, not a full pronunciation rebus. Generic fibers may need teaching and do not distinguish atrial from ventricular contexts. No muscle behavior, rhythm trace or disease mechanism is asserted.

entries.cue: Recognizable white wolf occupying a parking bay outlined by familiar floor lines.
entries.cue_scope: Wolff plus parking/Parkinson plus White learned name reminder; not an exact full-name sound rebus
entries.prior: New composition of familiar animal, color and parking relationship; no matching whole-term cue located in prior chapter banks/catalog/workshops checked.
entries.reason: User-proposed parking bay adds a familiar relationship without a prop pile. Parking is a partial learned association, not exact Parkinson phonetics. Recognition and full-name recovery are untested; no accessory-pathway anatomy or stand-alone diagnosis.
Prior hold preserved. No economical improved name bridge identified; disconnected fragments are not promoted merely to fill this bank.
